recommendations.title: `_optional_decision_text()` in `plan_tool/roadmap_artifacts.py` (step 2 "Extend DecisionRow parsing and rendering") only
recommendations.body: `_optional_decision_text()` in `plan_tool/roadmap_artifacts.py` (step 2 "Extend DecisionRow parsing and rendering") only checks `field not in raw`, not `raw[field] is None`, so an explicit `source: null` (or, on an inherited row, `rationale: null`) crashes with an opaque "must be a string, got NoneType" error instead of parsing as absent, unlike every other optional-field helper in the module (`_optional_row_text`, `_optional_id_list`, `_optional_product`, etc., all of which treat "absent or null" identically)
recommendations.suggested_action: change `_optional_decision_text()` to `if field not in raw or raw[field] is None: return None`, mirroring `_optional_row_text()`

recommendations.title: `tests/test_roadmap_artifacts.py` under-covers the decision-row contract the detail names: `test_roadmap_derived_decisio
recommendations.body: `tests/test_roadmap_artifacts.py` under-covers the decision-row contract the detail names: `test_roadmap_derived_decision_requires_existing_deliberation_fields()` asserts only that a Roadmap-derived row missing `rationale` fails to parse, never that one missing `rejected_alternatives` does too (despite the test's own detail-stated purpose covering both); and no test anywhere supplies an inherited row with a present, non-empty `rationale`/`rejected_alternatives` to prove that content round-trips rather than only proving its *absence* round-trips
recommendations.suggested_action: extend `test_roadmap_derived_decision_requires_existing_deliberation_fields()` with a `rejected_alternatives`-deletion case (or a parametrized variant), and add a case to `test_decision_rows_round_trip_for_inherited_and_roadmap_derived_forms()` (or a new test) where the inherited row keeps its `rationale`/`rejected_alternatives` instead of deleting them

recommendations.body:
the detail's `## Implementation` section attributes the compatibility-preserving caller `DecisionRowPayload.to_row` to `plan_tool/roadmap_candidate.py`, but that class actually lives in `plan_tool/roadmap_revision.py:DecisionRowPayload.to_row` (`roadmap_candidate.py` instead has an unrelated `_parse_stage_row()` that constructs `DecisionRow` positionally); the code itself is unaffected and compatibility is genuinely preserved either way, so this is a citation error in the detail, not a code gap

## Redirect

- **Reason**: the detail's `## Implementation` section names `plan_tool/roadmap_candidate.py:DecisionRowPayload.to_row` as an existing caller to preserve compatibility with, but that symbol is actually defined at `plan_tool/roadmap_revision.py:DecisionRowPayload.to_row`; no code edit is implied since compatibility already holds regardless of the citation
- **Suggested next**: detail --reconcile
